goal: [specialist:config_builder] Using DuckDB only, investigate how predicate selectivity affects query time: compare a very selective filter (returning roughly 0.1% of rows) against a broad one (roughly 10% of rows) on a table of about one million rows. Report the timings and whether more selective means meaningfully faster.

name: list_categories
list_templates

content: quack_selectivity is closest match; let me check it.

name: get_template
result:
{
  "name": "quack_selectivity",
  "content": "meta:
  name: "Quack Selectivity: does attach mode push predicates down?"
  description: >
    Closes the open boundary from the execution-modes study, whose query had
    no WHERE clause. The selectivity suite filters to a different fraction of
    rows per query (0.1%–20%). The question: is attach-mode cost FLAT across
    selectivity (it streams the whole table and filters client-side — the
    streaming-scan mechanism, now under filtering) or does it TRACK selectivity
    (it pushes the predicate to the server)? In-process DuckDB and pushdown are
    the references; Postgres is included as a row-store comparison. Postgres
    gets a B-tree index on selectivity_code (its natural tool for selective
    lookups, applied at ingestion outside the timed query loop); DuckDB/Quack
    are columnar and rely on automatic min-max zonemaps — each engine at its
    best. Identical data, identical SQL, cold cache, replication 5.

dataset:
  source: sql_benchmarks.plugins.data_sources.declarative_gen
  seed: 42
  tables:
    skewed_data:
      rows: rows
      columns:
        - name: id
          provider: sequence
          primary_key: true
        - name: selectivity_code
          provider: choice
          options: ["sel_0_1", "sel_1", "sel_5", "sel_10", "sel_20", "filler"]
          weights: [0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.639]
        - name: payload
          provider: text_concat
          prefix: "PADDING_DATA_TO_FORCE_REAL_SCAN_COST_AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA_"
          source: id
      indexes:
        - name: idx_skewed_selectivity_code
          columns: [selectivity_code]

definitions:
  rows:
    medium: 1_000_000
    large: 10_000_000

execution:
  test_suite: selectivity
  engines:
    - duckdb
    - quack
    - quack_pushdown
    - postgres
  replication: 5
  matrix:
    rows:
      - medium
      - large
",
  "path": "queue/quack_selectivity.yaml"
}

arguments.config_yaml:
meta:
  name: "DuckDB Selectivity: 0.1% vs 10% filter on 1M rows"
  description: >
    Investigates how predicate selectivity affects query time in DuckDB.
    Compares a highly selective filter (~0.1% of rows, selectivity_code =
    'sel_0_1') against a broad filter (~10% of rows, selectivity_code =
    'sel_10') on a table of one million rows. Identical data, identical
    engine (DuckDB in-process), cold cache, replication 5. Reports whether
    the more selective predicate is meaningfully faster thanks to DuckDB's
    automatic min-max zonemaps / columnar scan pruning.

dataset:
  source: sql_benchmarks.plugins.data_sources.declarative_gen
  seed: 42
  tables:
    skewed_data:
      rows: rows
      columns:
        - name: id
          provider: sequence
          primary_key: true
        - name: selectivity_code
          provider: choice
          options: ["sel_0_1", "sel_1", "sel_5", "sel_10", "sel_20", "filler"]
          weights: [0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.639]
        - name: payload
          provider: text_concat
          prefix: "PADDING_DATA_TO_FORCE_REAL_SCAN_COST_AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA_"
          source: id
      indexes:
        - name: idx_skewed_selectivity_code
          columns: [selectivity_code]

definitions:
  rows:
    medium: 1_000_000

execution:
  test_suite: selectivity
  engines:
    - duckdb
  replication: 5
  matrix:
    rows:
      - medium
